$comment: Nine exact Roman daily appointments reviewed against the pinned Brenton VPL and published source labels. Source wording remains in the pinned cache. These excerpts do not certify the excluded chapters for general reference conversion. No lectionary wording is copied.

daily|Psalm 145:8–9; 145:15–16; 145:17–1.boundaryReview: Brenton 144:8-9,15-18 retain the appointed mercy, care, food, open hands, justice and nearness clauses under these exact integer labels. The separate source 13a is outside this selection. The ordinary importer still withholds the complete lettered chapter.

daily|Psalm 145:10–11; 145:12–13ab; 145:.boundaryReview: The thanksgiving, kingdom, power and everlasting dominion clauses end at Brenton 144:13. The source's separate 13a faithful/loving clause corresponds to the unappointed Roman 145:13cd and is excluded, preserving the requested omission before17-18.

daily|Psalm 145:2–3; 145:4–5; 145:6–7.boundaryReview: Brenton 144:2-7 retain the daily blessing, greatness, generations, glory, mighty acts and goodness clauses in the same ordered integer source units. No title or suffix unit is requested.

daily|Psalm 145:8–9; 145:10–11; 145:12–1.boundaryReview: Roman145:13ab is Brenton144:13's everlasting kingdom/dominion, while Roman145:13cd is the separately printed Brenton144:13a faithful/loving clause. Both original source units are retained exactly once, with13a as a distinct printed witness before14; neither suffix is discarded or relabeled as a new integer verse.

daily|Psalm 145:17–18; 145:19–20; 145:21.boundaryReview: Brenton144:17-21 retain justice, nearness, fulfilled desire, preservation and final praise in the appointed order. These integer units are independently readable despite the unrelated earlier13a source label.

daily|Psalm 145:2–3; 145:8–9; 145:17–18.boundaryReview: Brenton144:2-3,8-9,17-18 retain the daily blessing/greatness, mercy/goodness and justice/nearness clauses; all intervening source units remain omitted as appointed.

daily|Psalm 116:12–13; 116:17–18.boundaryReview: Brenton115:3-4 contain the repayment/cup clauses of Roman116:12-13; Brenton115:8-9 contain sacrifice/invocation/vows of Roman116:17-18. Printed115:4a is an earlier repetition of the vows, corresponding to the omitted116:14, so it remains excluded. The source115 inventory still has no integer5 and is not declared complete.

daily|Psalm 13:6ab–6ab; 13:6cd–6cd.boundaryReview: Roman13:6's trust/joy clauses occur in Brenton12:5, while its sing/benefaction clauses occur in Brenton12:6. Both source verses are needed; source6's closing praise is retained as a whole-verse envelope. Selecting source6 alone would omit the appointed trust and salvation clauses.

daily|Psalm 139:1–3; 139:13–14ab; 139:23.boundaryReview: Brenton138:1-3 retain searching/knowing, sitting/rising, distant thoughts, path and all ways within those exact source units. Its138:3 already ends with all ways, unlike the Douay-Rheims boundary that requires its verse4. Brenton138:13-14 and23-24 retain the remaining appointed formation, thanksgiving and searched-heart/eternal-way clauses, keeping full14.

12.boundaryReview: The full native12 body retains the how-long/face clause in1, counsel/sorrow/enemy in2, hearing/light/death in3, enemy/rejoicing in4, trust/mercy/salvation in5, and sing/benefaction in6, covering all Standard13:1-6. Source1 keeps its printed title. Source6 additionally praises the name of the Most High; retain that exact closing wording with a wider-unit notice. This complete-body approval does not change the generic or partial Psalm13 mapping, including the existing exact Roman split ending review.

114.boundaryReview: Read the entire published native114 body: love/heard voice in1, inclined ear/calling in2, death/distress in3, name/deliverance in4, mercy/righteousness in5, protecting the simple/salvation in6, returned rest/benefaction in7, rescued life/eyes/feet in8, and the living land in9 correspond to Standard116:1-9. Preserve the printed Alleluia in source1. This is the complete first Greek source Psalm, not a new partial Standard116 offset rule.

115.boundaryReview: The literal published body has1-4,4a,6-10 and no integer5. Source1-4 retain belief/speech, human falsehood, repayment and the cup/name, corresponding to Standard116:10-13. Printed4a supplies the earlier vows-before-all-people clause of Standard116:14; preserve it as its own witness addressed to native4a, never manufacture verse5. Source6-10 retain precious death, the servant and loosened bonds, sacrifice/invocation, the later vows, and temple courts/Jerusalem, corresponding to Standard116:15-19. The printed Alleluia stays at source1. This full native115 group may be requested separately; requesting all Standard116 also requires the independently reviewed native114 group. No partial verse-offset rules are approved.

144.boundaryReview: The full native144 body retains every original integer row1-21, covering the complete praise, greatness, generations, works, mercy, kingdom, support, food, justice, nearness, salvation and final-blessing body of Standard145:1-21. Retain the separately printed13a faithful/loving clause between13 and14 as a distinct witness, with a wider-unit notice because it is additional to this Standard body group. Printed title and all Greek source variants remain intact. The importer still withholds this lettered chapter and the nine exact Roman excerpt reviews remain separately scoped.
